summary: Frontend-only verification of the new 'Payment Date Checkers' country navigation and 5 country pages, plus regression of the US Social Security calculator on the homepage. All requested testids are present, all interactive flows work, and no runtime error / blank-page regression from the earlier 'HeaderCountryNav is not defined' issue was observed.
critical_code_review_comments: CountryNav.jsx: The 'United States' entry inside the header dropdown (header-country-nav-us) links to '/', which is fine, but note the item testid pattern uses `header-${c.testid}` so it becomes `header-country-nav-us` (matches request). No change needed.
CountryPage.jsx: UkSelector uses `Math.min(4, Math.floor(n / 20))` which correctly maps 00-99 to 5 buckets; single-digit inputs (length 1) are ignored by requirement (requires 2 digits). Good.
countryData.js: Australia intentionally omits a schedule table (no scheduleRows), so `[data-testid="country-schedule-table"]` is correctly not rendered.
App.js is ~1000 lines - carry-over comment from iteration 2; consider splitting Calculator/ResultCard/ScheduleTable/FAQ for maintainability.
Testids used are pattern-consistent; consider adding a specific `data-testid="country-heading"` on the h1/title for future SEO/heading validation (nice-to-have).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Header dropdown item testids follow the pattern `header-${COUNTRIES[i].testid}` (e.g., header-country-nav-canada). Radix DropdownMenu needs ~300-500ms after clicking the trigger before items are queryable/visible. UK NI mapping: 00-19 Mon, 20-39 Tue, 40-59 Wed, 60-79 Thu, 80-99 Fri (verified with 05, 25, 42, 65, 85). Australia page has NO schedule table by design. Country pages have trailing slashes in their routes. Homepage calculator with default birth_date 1960-04-15 + benefit_type=standard returns 'Wednesday, July 15, 2026' at container time (July 2026).
rca of the issue: No bugs found. During the first pass, a transient MISSING result for country-us-checker-link and calculator-submit result was observed due to querying immediately after a client-side navigation/click without allowing React to re-render + API to respond. A follow-up run with slightly longer waits confirmed both work correctly. This is not a product bug.
